body.p: Claims 1-8 are pending in the present application. Claims 1-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as being directed to an abstract idea without significantly more. Claims 1-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2020/0292322 to Ozog in view of KR 2022/0089772 to Kim. Reconsideration of this application is respectfully requested in view of remarks and amendments submitted herewith.

The undersigned thanks Examiner Nguyen for the telephonic interview of September 18, 2024. The claims of the subject application were discussed in view of the 35 U.S.C. § 101 rejection and the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejection. A tentative agreement was reached regarding proposed amendments, which are formally presented herein, to overcome the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejection. However, no agreement was reached regarding the 35 U.S.C. §101 rejection. However, the Examiner indicated that an updated search and consideration would be required.
Entry of this statement of substance of interview is requested as this statement is in compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.133.

Applicant respectfully requests that claims 1-2 and 4-8 be amended. Claim 9 has been newly added. Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures, and claims as originally filed. It is believed that no new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as being directed to an abstract idea without significantly more. The rejection is respectfully traversed.

Independent claim 1 has been amended to recite acquiring driving environment information and driving state information related to the autonomous driving, including an occurrence of rapid acceleration or deceleration of the autonomous driving vehicle to determine a vehicle control state,

a driving route undertaken by the autonomous driving vehicle, and a driving position of the autonomous driving vehicle when the vehicle control state becomes a particular state that includes rapid steering or evacuation driving or the rapid acceleration or deceleration; determining one or more request questions for requesting an answer from the passenger from among one or more managed questions based on the driving environment information and the driving state information, wherein the one or more request questions includes at least one question related to a specific scene encountered during the autonomous traveling by the autonomous driving vehicle, and at least one question unaffected by the specific scene encountered during the autonomous traveling by the autonomous driving vehicle; and transmitting the one or more request questions at a predetermined timing in response to determining a time at which the autonomous driving vehicle is caused to autonomously arrive at a destination from the acquired driving state information.

As now amended, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1, 7, and 8 recite subject matter that is not directed to an abstract idea, and is rather integrated into a practical application and adds significantly more to the alleged abstract idea by providing technical improvements, and thus the claims are eligible.

Contrary to the Office Action's position that the features of independent claims 1, 7, and 8 recite limitations that cover mental processes (Office Action at p. 4), independent claims 1, 7, and 8 now affirmatively recites not only the operations being performed by one or more processors of the server of the questionnaire apparatus, but also acquiring information to determine a vehicle control state, a driving route undertaken by the autonomous driving vehicle, and a driving position of the autonomous driving vehicle when the vehicle control state becoming a particular state that includes rapid steering, or evacuation, or the rapid acceleration or deceleration; as well as a particular implementation of when to transmit the one or more request questions (here, at a predetermined timing at which the autonomous driving vehicle is caused to autonomously arrive at a destination from the acquired driving state information). Such features do not reasonably constitute mental processes, as asserted by the Office Action at p. 4, which is an overgeneralization of the claims.
Moreover, amended independent claims 1, 7, and 8 recite more than just mental steps that do not integrate the alleged abstract idea into a practical application (Office Action at p. 4). Rather,

these claims have been amended to specifically recite patent-eligible details by imposing meaningful limits on practicing the alleged abstract idea by reciting not only the presence of one or more processors of a server of a questionnaire apparatus to carry out particular operations, but also taking into account an affirmative and tangible action performed by the one or more processors in response to determining a time at which the autonomous driving vehicle is caused to autonomously arrive at a destination from the acquired driving state information. More particularly, meaningful limits on practicing the alleged abstract idea are recited in independent claims 1, 7, and 8 so that the claims cannot be merely interpreted as failing to integrate the alleged abstract idea into a practical application, but rather, in response to determining a time at which the autonomous driving vehicle is caused to autonomously arrive at a destination from the acquired driving state information, the one or more processors transmit the one or more request questions, the one or more request questions includes at least one question related to a specific scene encountered during the autonomous traveling by the autonomous driving vehicle, and at least one question unaffected by the specific scene encountered during the autonomous traveling by the autonomous driving vehicle.

Still further, when the claims are viewed as an ordered combination and as a whole, they recite significantly more than the alleged abstract idea. As explained in the subject specification (for example, paragraph [0012] of the as-filed specification), the questionnaire includes one or more questions related to a particular scene affected by the driving environment or a driving state of the vehicle, and one or more questions that are not affected by a scene. In addition, the questionnaire apparatus changes one or more questions to request an answer from the passenger in accordance with the driving environment or the driving state of the vehicle. Specifically, the questionnaire apparatus determines one or more questions for requesting an answer from the passenger among one or more questions managed by the evaluation apparatus based on the information about the driving environment or the information about the driving state, to then carry out a questionnaire composed of one or more appropriate questions while reducing the number of the questions (for example, paragraph [0016] of the as-filed specification). Therefore, amended independent claims 1, 7, and 8 recite subject matter that integrates the alleged abstract idea into a practical application and amounts to significantly more than the alleged abstract idea.
Withdrawal of the rejection and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.
Claims 1-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ozog in view of Kim. The rejection is respectfully traversed.

The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. KSR, 550 U.S. at 416, 82 USPQ2d at 1395; Sakraida v. AG Pro, Inc., 425 U.S. 273, 282, 189 USPQ 449, 453 (1976); Anderson's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co., 396 U.S. 57, 62- 63, 163 USPQ 673, 675 (1969); Great Atl. & P. Tea Co. v. Supermarket Equip. Corp., 340 U.S. 147, 152, 87 USPQ 303, 306 (1950). Further, "a prior art reference must be considered in its entirety, i.e., as a whole, including portions that would lead away from the claimed invention." W.L. Gore & Assoc., Inc. v. Garlock, Inc., 721 F.2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert. denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984).

As tentatively agreed during the interview, Applicant respectfully submits that Ozog in view of Kim fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1. Specifically, Ozog in view of Kim fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1 regarding acquiring driving environment information and driving state information related to the autonomous driving, including an occurrence of rapid acceleration or deceleration of the autonomous driving vehicle to determine a vehicle control state, a driving route undertaken by the autonomous driving vehicle, and a driving position of the autonomous driving vehicle when the vehicle control state becomes a particular state that includes rapid steering or evacuation driving or the rapid acceleration or deceleration; determining one or more request questions for requesting an answer from the passenger from among one or more managed questions based on the driving environment information and the driving state information, wherein the one or more request questions includes at least one question related to a specific scene encountered during the autonomous traveling by the autonomous driving vehicle, and at least one question unaffected by the specific scene encountered during the autonomous traveling by the autonomous driving vehicle; and transmitting the one or more request questions at a predetermined timing in response to determining a time at which the autonomous driving
vehicle is caused to autonomously arrive at a destination from the acquired driving state information, and as similarly amended in independent claims 7 and 8.

Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1, 7, and 8, and all claims that depend therefrom, can no longer be rejected as being unpatentable over Ozog in view of Kim. Further, Kim fails to cure the deficiencies of Nagaoka and Ozog.
Withdrawal of the rejection and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested. New Dependent Claim 9

New dependent claim 9 has been added to depend upon independent claim 1. For the reasons stated above in relation to independent claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that new dependent claim 9 is patentable over the cited references for at least the reasons presented above with respect to independent claim 1, and for the respective subject matter recited in this claim.
Consideration of new dependent claim 9 is respectfully requested.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response. Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.

No additional fees are believed to be due. However, the Director is hereby authorized to charge all required fees (including any extension of time fees) and to credit any overpayment of fees in this and any concurrent or future correspondence to Deposit Account No. 041133.
